subject: Cert roadmap — phases, evidence expectations, and FedRAMP sequencing
messages:
From: Eli Jenkins <eli.jenkins@acmecloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com, SaaSify Security <security@saasify.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify Redwood's certification sequencing & what evidence we'll get during diligence

Hi Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we start our procurement review, we want to map Redwood's certification roadmap into our timeline. A couple quick things we need clarified so we can update our security committee: 

- Does Redwood intend to pursue ISO 27001 certification before or after FedRAMP tailoring work? We have internal guidance that favors ISO first but need to understand sequencing implications.
- For SOC 2 Type 2, can you share the most recent snapshot report and confirm which control families are out-of-scope for third-party hosting customers?
- For FedRAMP readiness: do you expect to target FedRAMP Moderate or Low initially, and do you anticipate needing an agency sponsor (or will you pursue a JAB path)?

If you can attach any high-level roadmap (milestones + expected quarters) and a short list of typical evidence artifacts you provide (policies, configuration exports, audit logs, encryption attestations), that would help speed review.

Appreciate it — can you get something by next Tue (10th)? Our review deadline is end of month.

Thanks,
Eli Jenkins
Head of Cloud Security
Acme Cloud Services


From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Eli Jenkins <eli.jenkins@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Redwood's certification sequencing & what evidence we'll get during diligence

Hi Eli —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary up front: our current plan is ISO 27001 certification in H2 2026 with FedRAMP alignment work starting in parallel in early 2027; target FedRAMP Moderate via agency-sponsored ATO. Ive attached a short snapshot of our SOC 2 Type 2 and a proposed scope matrix for ISO to this thread.

Short answers to your bullets: 
- Sequence: ISO first (controls baseline and ISMS), FedRAMP after (because FedRAMP will reuse ISO/SOC evidence but adds federal-specific artifacts and continuous monitoring). Doing ISO first reduces remediations during FedRAMP scoping.
- SOC 2: attached PDF is our latest Type 2 (covering period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31). Hosting customers can expect most common security and availability controls; a few org-level controls (e.g., legal/compliance attestations) are out of scope. I'll call out specifics below.
- FedRAMP: were planning Moderate and expect to pursue agency-sponsored ATO. JAB is a longer runway and not on our near-term roadmap.

Attachments in this reply: SOC2-Type2-snapshot-2025.pdf, ISO27001-scope-matrix.xlsx

Next steps I propose: 
1) Marissa (controls lead) to enumerate the 6 most-requested artifacts for diligence and owner names.
2) Rishi (security ops) to provide the log-retention and audit-log export sample and confirm retention windows for dedicated vs hosted customers.
3) Marcus (compliance program) to sketch draft quarter-level milestones for ISO and FedRAMP and any key gating dependencies (third-party attestation, penetration testing cadence).

We can have a short 30-min sync to walk your committee through the attachments if helpful — Wed or Thu next week works for us.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0122

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Eli Jenkins <eli.jenkins@acmecloud.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Redwood's certification sequencing & what evidence we'll get during diligence

Hi Eli —

Following up with the artifacts list we typically provide for procurement security reviews. Short list first (we can expand as needed):

1) SOC 2 Type 2 report (attached) — scope: security & availability; exclusions: legal department controls and certain HR hiring background-check records are not provided for privacy reasons.
2) ISMS charter + top-level policies (InfoSec policy, access control, incident response).
3) Network diagram + segmentation summary (redacted).
4) Audit log export sample (S3-presigned link or CSV with redaction). Rishi will confirm the export format and retention window.
5) Pen test summary report + remediation timeline (we provide executive summary; detailed vuln lists require an NDA).
6) Encryption configuration and KMS attestation (for customer-managed keys we provide KMS integration docs).

I'll flag owners and ETA: 
- SOC 2 / policies: Marissa — attached now.
- Logs / retention: Rishi — ETA 2/5.
- Roadmap milestones / FedRAMP sequencing: Marcus — ETA 2/6.

If you want a single zip of redacted artifacts + one-pager milestone timeline I can assemble that and share via our secure drive link.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Lead, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

>

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Eli Jenkins <eli.jenkins@acmecloud.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify Redwood's certification sequencing & what evidence we'll get during diligence

Eli —

Per Marissa's list, attached are the answers and the sample audit export link. A few clarifications for your security committee: 

- Audit logs: we export CloudWatch logs + application audit events. Retention defaults: hosted customers = 90 days (configurable via paid plan), dedicated = 365 days by contract. We provide a redacted CSV sample (link below) and can produce longer windows for customers with contractual requirements.
- ISO scope matrix: the attached spreadsheet highlights in-scope services (API gateway, inference runtime, control plane). Data classification for customer data is listed; Redwood does not persist customer prompt content beyond configured retention windows unless opted-in for analytics.
- FedRAMP sequencing: pursuing ISO first reduces duplicated control work because our ISMS will formalize policies and control owners up-front. For Moderate, agency sponsorship is our expected route — this reduces upfront cost for customers and aligns with our enterprise go-to-market.

Secure links: 
- Redacted audit sample (S3 presigned): https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-samples/redacted-audit-sample.csv?X-Amz-Example
- Roadmap draft (GDrive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Baa-example

If the committee wants to see the SOC 2 testing matrix mapped to ISO controls, we can produce a short crosswalk. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
